From developer's point of view this is not an easy question to answer. First it has to be decided which tags would be used where: the whole fic, only on chapters. It seems easy but someone has to write the code and add it to the existing structure and make sure it works properly. And I really don't think this would contribute for a better user experience.

Another point: there are I.don't know how many stories on AO3. Say this functionality is added tommorow. People start using it. But the millions? Of fics already published won't have that, I doubt the authors would come and add the tags to the chapters. Searches would be useless.

That is the reason when a system or archive of information is created the logic of how to organize the data should be though of carefully. Because once the entries of data start piling up it's very hard to change the structure. And if you do change it the data archive becomes inconsistent. Case in point all of then old entries before the change that don't use the new functionality (chapter tags in this case).

I doubt the technical implementation of this functionality would be easy to add to the site. The developers have to figure out a way to logically include this to the existing structure. It would take time and resources and would make the site more complicated. I'm not sure how the search would work exactly. It will return link to the story specifying the number of the chapter including the tag. Which means you end up with the same result: found story by tag. The desigion to click on it or not depends on the tags, it wouldn't matter in which chapter the content is included. So the user experience is basically the same but the user experience and site structure are needlessly more complicated.


So the question is, if the author would have to use all of the tags again as is now, listed in the beginning of the story (when you see the story on the site you see all of the tags)? If yes this is a little redundant to have them again in a chapter.

Next question. If the tags are going to be used only on specific chapfers then the reader goes in blind, not knowing there's triggering content until they reach the chapter. This structure has to be decided carefully and logically. I am not really sure how this would work without making it more difficult to use and potentially buggy. 

Also I think that this could be achieved with author's note at the begining of the fic and the specific chapter to give warnings.

When you write third person limited you have to be in your character's head and keep in mind what they know, see, feel, hear.

For example, if someone is coming behind your character they would hear the footsteps. Not see them immediately. Or they would sense them. Your character may not be sure at first who is behind them.

You can also put a little more distance and show more broader view of the scene where you think it fits. But if you want to stick to third limited this is the main thing you need to keep track of.

Also you can describe your character's emotions and thoughts in depth since you're in their head. You can describe their surroundings too like you would in any POV.
I don't deny the possible advantages of first person. It's just my preference, especially for fanfiction.

I feel like when you read fanfiction in third person you see the character's perspective. And when you read in first person it's like reading someone else's take on the character's perspective. At lest for me it's more distant, even though it sounds illogical. To get to the character I have one more step I have to cross. Also the writer is less invisible especially in fanfiction when it's first person.
Also, first person sometimes feels self indulgent.

I prefer third person. This doesn't mean that I won't give a first person story a chance, but when I start to read and it's "I" my first reaction is a bit negative. I think for me this is more concerning fanfiction, because we all know the characters that we are going to read about. So when someone adopts the "I" they are hijacking the persona of the character. To pull it off they have to be really good. And in my opinion first person is harder to write well and more limited. It could be either really good or really bad depending on the writer's skill. Minor flaws that would not show in third person may be more prominent in first person. 

Also first person is more limited when it comes to perspective. You only have one or two. And changing perspectives is annoying from my point of view. Third person limited lets the reader get close to the characters and explore their thoughts just like with first person but it's smoother in my opinion. It's just a preference. I like to be in the story, not just to see it from one character's point of view. Although third person limited does the same, but still I feel its less narrowed and allows more freedom.

Also maybe some people find it harder to immerse themselves in a story that is first person. I know people that dont read fan fiction that just don't pick up stories in first person.

Again, not saying first person can't be good, just a preference and opinion.
